segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. JavaScript language-level globals unrelated to any browser API.

caveats: Skips the `ToNumber` coercion real JS applies — a non-number argument (reachable via `any`) is treated as already numeric, so `isNaN('hello' as any)` is `false` (Node: `true`).
Skips `ToNumber` coercion like `isNaN` — a non-number argument (via `any`) isn't coerced, diverging from Node's `isFinite('x')`.
`String()` with no argument is `""`, not real JS's `"undefined"` (a genuinely absent value doesn't arise in typed code — [ADR-00291](../adr/ADR-00291.md))
notes: Routes through the template-literal renderer; an `any` input dispatches on its runtime tag
JS ToNumber: whole-string parse (`"12px"` → `NaN`, unlike `parseFloat`), `""`/whitespace → 0, `"0x10"` → 16, boolean → 0/1, `null` → 0; a numeric input passes through unchanged (exact i64 stays i64)

Only the exact word `"Infinity"` (optionally signed) is `Infinity`; C's `"inf"`/`"infinity"`/case variants are `NaN`, matching real JS ([ADR-00291](../adr/ADR-00291.md)/[ADR-00529](../adr/ADR-00529.md))
Shared truthiness (`NaN`, `""`, 0 falsy — [ADR-00116](../adr/ADR-00116.md))
A no-digits input returns a real `NaN` (endptr-checked, double result — [ADR-00287](../adr/ADR-00287.md))

With `radix` omitted, auto-detects base 16 for a `"0x"`/`"0X"` prefix (`"0xFF"` → `255`) and base 10 otherwise — no octal auto-detect (`"077"` → `77`), and `"0x"` with no trailing hex digit is `NaN`, matching real JS ([ADR-00530](../adr/ADR-00530.md))
A `"0x"` hex prefix reads only its leading `0` → `0` (real parseFloat, unlike `Number("0x10")` → `16`) via `__kml_strtod_parsefloat` ([ADR-00545](../adr/ADR-00545.md))

A no-conversion input returns a real `NaN`; the only accepted infinity spelling is the exact word `"Infinity"` (`"inf"`/case variants → `NaN`) ([ADR-00287](../adr/ADR-00287.md)/[ADR-00529](../adr/ADR-00529.md))

caveats: `let NaN = 99;` is a reserved-name collision under the default `-compat=strict`; `-compat=js` allows the shadow real JS permits
notes: `NaN != x`/`!== x` comparisons are correct — compiled as unordered `fcmp une`, so `NaN !== NaN` is `true` as in JS — see [ADR-00188](../adr/ADR-00188.md)

caveats: Same shadowing caveat as `NaN` above — needs `-compat=js`, not unconditional

notes: As a literal value
`globalThis.X` (and nested/call forms like `globalThis.JSON.stringify(...)`, `globalThis.setTimeout(...)`) desugars to the bare ambient global X ([ADR-00508](../adr/ADR-00508.md))
caveats: Only member access resolves, and only to *known* globals — an unknown `globalThis.foo` is a compile error (there is no dynamic global record); a bare `globalThis` used as a standalone object value, computed access (`globalThis["x"]`), and assigning a new global (`globalThis.x = …`) are unsupported

notes: Leaves the unreserved *and* reserved (`;/?:@&=+$,#`) character sets unescaped. See [ADR-00024](../adr/ADR-00024.md).
A malformed escape (a lone/truncated `%`, or one not followed by two hex digits) throws a real `URIError` as in JS ([ADR-00556](../adr/ADR-00556.md))

Does **not** decode a `%XX` escape representing a reserved character (leaves it as literal `%XX` text) — the one real behavioral difference from `decodeURIComponent`. See [ADR-00024](../adr/ADR-00024.md).
Leaves only the unreserved set (letters, digits, `-_.!~*'()`) unescaped. See [ADR-00024](../adr/ADR-00024.md).
Decodes every valid `%XX` escape unconditionally; a malformed escape throws a real `URIError` as in JS ([ADR-00556](../adr/ADR-00556.md)). See [ADR-00024](../adr/ADR-00024.md).
Base64 decode

WHATWG forgiving-base64: ASCII whitespace is stripped, a missing-padding trailing 2-/3-char group still decodes, and a remaining length ≡ 1 (mod 4) throws `InvalidCharacterError` ([ADR-00550](../adr/ADR-00550.md))

After the up-to-two trailing `=` are stripped, an interior or excess `=` in the data region throws `InvalidCharacterError` — `=` is accepted only as trailing padding, matching real atob ([ADR-00563](../adr/ADR-00563.md))
Operates byte-for-byte on the input string (this compiler's strings are already plain byte sequences — no separate "binary string" type needed). See [ADR-00024](../adr/ADR-00024.md).
An input character outside the base64 alphabet throws a real `InvalidCharacterError` DOMException, matching WHATWG atob ([ADR-00458](../adr/ADR-00458.md))
Base64 encode, `=`-padded (RFC 4045). See [ADR-00024](../adr/ADR-00024.md).

caveats: `EventEmitter`/`URL`/`URLSearchParams`/functions/class instances/`Promise`/`any`/`unknown` are rejected at compile time rather than silently aliased (`URL` matches Node, which throws `DataCloneError` for it); a `Map`/`Set` with an **array/Map/Set** key or value element type is also rejected (only scalar/string/object elements clone — [ADR-00574](../adr/ADR-00574.md)). A plain `ArrayBuffer` is byte-copied, a `SharedArrayBuffer` passes by reference, and an `Error` (or subtype) copies its kind/message/name ([ADR-00591](../adr/ADR-00591.md)); a cloned `AggregateError`'s `.errors` degrades to empty
notes: Real recursive deep copy, dispatched entirely on the argument's static type (arrays, incl. nested/TypedArrays, plain objects, and `Map`/`Set` recurse, cloning every entry deeply — [ADR-00574](../adr/ADR-00574.md); scalars pass through as value types) — see [ADR-00113](../adr/ADR-00113.md)

caveats: Drained at the reachable checkpoints (end of the top-level script, each scheduler step); a program with neither timers nor async tasks drains once at exit
notes: A FIFO of callback closures, run after the current synchronous script and before timers ([TDD-00083](../tdd/TDD-00083.md) Stage 3 / [ADR-00245](../adr/ADR-00245.md))

caveats: A no-op under `-mm=manual` (the default) — nothing is ever collected; only meaningful under `-mm=gc`, where it forces a full Boehm collection
notes: The Node `--expose-gc` `global.gc()` idiom; added to make weak-reference reclamation deterministically observable ([ADR-00349](../adr/ADR-00349.md))

General/dynamic `eval` is unimplemented (needs the opt-in embedded engine, [TDD-00046](../tdd/TDD-00046.md), not started). A narrow **static subset** does work: a compile-time-constant `eval("<expression>")` is compiled in place through this compiler's own parser+codegen, no engine — see [ADR-00198](../adr/ADR-00198.md). A dynamic string, a statement/declaration, or a reference to a top-level binding is a clean compile error, never a runtime throw (so it can't false-pass a negative test)
